content.text: don't wait for PCR: start IV acyclovir promptly until HSV and VZV encephalitis are excluded; continue usually 14 days or until these viruses are excluded; can cause LFT abnormalities, marrow suppression and transient renal failure; giving it IV slowly over 1 h w adequate hydration helps prevent nephrotoxicity.
Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) dose, herpes simplex encephalitis (adults and adolescents):
Adults and adolescents ≥12 y: 10 mg/kg IV infused at a constant rate over 1 h, every 8 h for 10 days. When dosage adjustments are required, base them on estimated CrCl.
Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) administration and renal safety:

IV infusion only — ⍉ topical, IM, PO, SC, or ocular. Infuse over ≥1 h to reduce risk of renal tubular damage. Renal failure, in some cases fatal, has been observed w acyclovir therapy. TTP/HUS, which has resulted in death, has occurred in immunocompromised pts receiving acyclovir. Adequate hydration must accompany IV infusion. Other nephrotoxic drugs, pre-existing renal dz, and dehydration make further renal impairment more likely.
~1% of pts on IV acyclovir show encephalopathic changes (lethargy, obtundation, tremors, confusion, hallucinations, agitation, seizures, coma).
Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) max dose, CI, interactions, OD:

Max dose ≤20 mg/kg every 8 h for any pt. CI: hypersensitivity to acyclovir or valacyclovir. Probenecid ↑ acyclovir half-life and AUC; urinary excretion and renal clearance correspondingly reduced. OD (ingestions up to 20 g reported): agitation, coma, seizures, lethargy. Acute renal failure w anuria may benefit from hemodialysis until renal function restored.
